title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page). G is an 'MD-graph', most likely a Mumford–Deligne (stable) graph indexing a boundary stratum of the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν}. S is the set of vertices, A the edges, \hat A the oriented (half-)edges, and G^b an auxiliary graph built from G. For each vertex s there is a two-element set E_s of local orientations (cyclic orders at a trivalent vertex). Their product \mathcal E(G) = ∏_s E_s is a torsor under r(G) = {±1}^S. Grothendieck builds an extension of groups (26): 0 → Z^{\hat A} → E(G) → r(G) → 0. He gets it by pushing out the 'square' extension 0 → Z^S --2--> Z^S → (Z/2)^S → 0 along the source map Z^S → Z^{\hat A} (giving E(G^b)), and then along (20). So each 'flip' of orientation at a vertex s lifts to an element whose square is the sum of the generators attached to the half-edges issuing from s. Read geometrically, this is a half-twist-type element whose square is a product of Dehn twists around the curves bounding the pair of pants at s.

This page. For any extension of groups 0 → L → E → Γ → 0 and any Γ-torsor P, one can form a groupoid E(P):
- objects: the elements of P;
- Hom(x,y): the fibre of E over the unique y−x ∈ Γ with y = x + (y−x);
- composition: the group law of E.

This is the connected groupoid with vertex group E, fibred over the indiscrete groupoid on P, with fibres L-torsors. In other words, it is the contracted product of the torsor P with the extension. Grothendieck applies this with E = E(G) and P = \mathcal E(G) and obtains the intrinsic description (28): S_0 T_G ≅ E(G)(\mathcal E(G)). He proposes (28) as the *definition* of S_0 T_G when G has modular dimension 0, i.e. G is a maximally degenerate trivalent graph and the stratum is a point.

In modern terms, S_0 T_G is the local fundamental groupoid of the moduli stack near a 0-dimensional boundary stratum. Its base points are the tangential-type base points indexed by vertex orientations. The vertex group is the extension of the orientation-flip group {±1}^S by the free abelian group of Dehn twists.

The left margin gives a variant: start from the extension E_S (23)/(27) at the level of S, form E_S(\mathcal E(G)), then push out along Z^S → Z^{\hat A}. The result is the same groupoid.

The page then moves to modular dimension 1, the first case being the M_{0,4} degeneration. The MD-graph has one edge a joining two vertices, each carrying two free ends. It corresponds to a 4-element set I with a partition of type (2,2), and equivalently to a 'combinatorial square' Q on I: I is the set of vertices of Q, and the partition is given by the diagonals. This is continued on the next page.
errors: The transcription's 'δ(G)' as the target of y−x should be r(G) (the group {±1}^S); the fibre is taken over y−x ∈ r(G).
Notational overloading rather than a mathematical error: \mathcal E(G) (the r(G)-torsor of vertex orientations) and E(G) (the group extension) are written almost identically.

Composition by the 'additive' law is legitimate here: r(G) = {±1}^S is abelian and E(G), built by pushout from Z^S --2--> Z^S, is abelian. In a non-abelian setting the order convention would need care.

Minor gap: the page does not check that the pushout along the source map gives the geometrically correct relation (the square of the flip at s equals the product of the twists along the edges at s). It is asserted by construction.

ideas.what: Groupoid attached to a group extension plus a torsor under the quotient: Ob = P, Hom(x,y) = fibre of E over y−x.
ideas.modern_name: Contracted product / groupoid induced from an extension and a torsor (a connected groupoid with prescribed vertex group fibred over an indiscrete groupoid)
ideas.where_published: Similar torsor/extension formalism in SGA 1 / Giraud; not this exact form

ideas.what: Defining the Teichmüller groupoid at a 0-dimensional boundary stratum (modular dimension 0) as an extension of the vertex-orientation group {±1}^S by Dehn twists Z^{\hat A}, with base points the vertex orientations.
ideas.modern_name: Local (orbifold) fundamental groupoid at a maximally degenerate point of \bar M_{g,n}, with tangential base points; half-twists and Dehn twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara–Nakamura, Nakamura (1990s); Bakalov–Kirillov Lego-Teichmüller game; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and its low-dimensional strata qualitatively, not this formula

ideas.what: Encoding the M_{0,4}-type degeneration (one edge, two trivalent vertices, four free ends) as a combinatorial square on the 4 ends, with the (2,2)-partition given by the diagonals.
ideas.modern_name: Dual graph of a boundary point of \bar M_{0,4}; cyclic structures and pants decompositions

missed.claim: An explicit closed formula S_0T_G ≅ E(G)(\mathcal E(G)) for the 0-skeleton Teichmüller groupoid, with base points the vertex orientations. The extension is obtained by pushing out the 'multiplication by 2' extension along the source map, so each orientation flip squares to the sum of edge twists at that vertex. This is a precise unpublished Grothendieck formulation, but its content matches later work on tangential base points (Nakamura, Bakalov–Kirillov).
missed.quote: On peut prendre (28) comme définition de S_0 T_G, pour G de dimension modulaire nulle.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents how Grothendieck intended to build the Teichmüller tower from the 0- and 1-dimensional strata, anticipating the later Lego-Teichmüller formalism.

deep.surprise_reason: The categorical construction is routine. The geometric content (Dehn twists plus orientation half-twists at maximally degenerate points) was developed independently in the later Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature. It is a nice archival detail, not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: 'fibre de E(G) en dessus de y−x ∈ δ(G)' should read 'fibre de E(G) au dessus de y−x ∈ r(G)'.
The underlined word in 'd'un ___ combinatoire de I' is 'carré', not 'cycle' (consistent with the next page: 'carré combinatoire Q').
Last lines: roughly 'Q (dont I est l'ens des sommets, et la partition celle des diagonales)', not 'l'un des sommets ... demi-graphes'.
'correspondant à la donnée d'un ensemble I des [bouts?] de cardinal 4': there is no exponent \mathbb I^I; the symbol is I with an overwritten letter.
Margin note, approximately: 'On peut aussi se donner d'abord E_G et E_S (27), d'où E_S(E(G)) [via] (23), Z^S --2--> Z^S, Z^S → Z^{\hat A}'. It describes the alternative construction by pushout.
